A1.justification: Both complete, readable 14-page PDFs describe Mantis and contain corresponding text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Twelve pages render identically; the differences on pages 1 and 4 are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO evaluations, real-world robot trials, DVF ablations and language-supervision experiments, including results in Tables 1–3 and 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation, real-world robot and ablation results, including the empirical evidence in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same architecture, objectives, progressive training and adaptive temporal ensemble. Figure 2 rearranges the displayed inputs, but the unchanged Equations (1) and (3) already list the visual input before the instruction; this does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both use SSV2, DROID and the same 38 language-supervision datasets. Evaluation coverage remains four LIBERO suites, three real-world scenarios with ID/OOD instructions, and MME, OCRBench and RealWorldQA.

E2.justification: The comparator sets are identical: the 12 baselines in Table 1, four convergence baselines in Figure 5, π0.5 in the real-world experiments, and Qwen2.5-VL, ECoT and ChatVLA in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Appendices A–C preserve all settings, preprocessing and metrics, including 30-epoch LIBERO fine-tuning, 50 trials per task, and 10 executions per real-world instruction with up to five consecutive attempts.

E4.justification: The DVF, residual-connection and pretraining ablations, TE-versus-ATE analysis, language-supervision ablations and qualitative examples are unchanged. Appendix D and Figures 9–10 retain the same supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Trial-count reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. Table 1 still reports Mantis success rates of 98.8, 99.2, 94.4 and 94.2, averaging 96.7; the ablation, multimodal and task-level results in Tables 2, 3 and 6 are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the training objectives and Appendix A's FLOPs expression and complexity analysis are unchanged. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about DVF, progressive training, language capabilities, 96.7% LIBERO success and approximately 50% fewer inference calls.

C2.justification: Interpretations of DVF, language supervision, convergence and ATE remain identical. Section 5 retains the limitation of motion rollbacks attributed to missing robot-state inputs and the same proposed future directions.

D1.justification: The front-page code link changes from zhijie-group/Mantis to SJTU-DENG-Lab/Mantis, updating the documented repository location. Implementation details are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish any change in available code or weights.

R1.justification: All 58 references and the related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to visual foresight, track guidance and latent-action supervision remains identical.

P1.justification: Xueqi Li's affiliation changes from SJTU/SII to SII/SUSTech, with corresponding affiliation renumbering. The version/date header also changes; the scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with image tokens before instruction tokens, a correspondingly repositioned visual-to-connector path, and small spacing changes. Its caption, components and other panels retain their content; all other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 now displays image and instruction inputs in the order already specified by Equations (1) and (3), resolving a small inconsistency in the method presentation. This is a limited improvement; the scientific evidence and claims are unchanged, and the repository-address update alone does not establish better resource availability.
